semantics: three search strategies over the same Phase-G candidate universe: Exhaustive (oracle), FixedHeuristic (constant per-frame plan), DsfbGuided (deterministic trust model: recent-winner active set, phi/omega/alpha diagnostics, regime broadening, deterministic rotating sweep; no stochastic bandits). DSFB is encoder-side only and never touches normative decode.
primary_criterion: N_dsfb < N_exhaustive while J_dsfb == J_exhaustive on steady content

steady_pan_64x64.content: 10x6 box gliding diagonally inside a 64x64 canvas over uniform 90

wrap_by_7_40x32.content: whole-canvas wrap scroll by 7 rows/frame (outside the fixed heuristic's 1..3 probe window)

static_blink_32x24.content: 16 static frames then 16 one-pixel blink frames

regime_32x32.content: static textured scene -> wrap-by-7 -> noise -> whole-scene vertical pan

notes: J_ratio = strategy stream bytes / exhaustive stream bytes (same court, same input raster).
N_ratio = total candidates evaluated / exhaustive total; work_ratio = pixel-scan work estimate ratio.
Local rebase events (whole-frame RAW captures) counted per strategy: frame > 0, winner family raw, object declaration bytes > 0.
Regime switches are located from the oracle winner-family sequence; guided recovery latency = frames after the switch until the guided winner equals the oracle winner for the rest of the segment.
DSFB diagnostics phi (explanatory quality), omega (drift EWMA) and alpha (regime / broaden armed) are sampled in the log and asserted in tests/phase_h.rs.
Phase-G encode paths are unchanged under EncoderStrategy::Exhaustive (the default); the unified reset candidate made the library scan content-addressed.
